Article Title: 'Plotting a super-tainted majority': Congress taunts Centre over delay in Parliament prorogation
Article Text:
File photo: Congress general secretary Jairam Ramesh

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Congress on Friday mounted its attack against the centre over the delay in prorogation of Parliament after it adjourned sine die, accusing the government of plotting a "super tainted two-third majority" to get the Delimitation Bill passed in Lok Sabha.In a social media post on X, Congress leader Jairam Ramesh said the gap between the adjournment of Parliament sine die and its prorogation has reached 29 days."So today the Modi govt has set a new record, bettering its own set in 2015. The gap between the adjournment of Parliament sine die and its prorogation has reached 29 days. The gap for the 2015 Monsoon Session was 28 days. The gap for the 2026 Monsoon Session is increasing by the day with no clear prospect for its early prorogation. Normally the gap is just three-four days," Jairam Ramesh said."It is abundantly clear that the Union home minister was severely wounded by the stunning defeat he had inflicted on himself and his govt with his staggering arrogance in the Lok Sabha on April 17, 2026. He is now plotting a comeback to secure a super-tainted two-thirds majority to get the Constitution Amendment Bill passed in the Lok Sabha. He has already engineered a split in three parties that had voted against the Bill on April 17, 2026, and is using threats, intimidation and incentives to get others (who had also voted against the Bill) to change their stance.The Union home minister does not have the numbers but his bravado, bluff and bluster will not let him read the writing on the wall," he added.The Congress leader said that the government is keeping the suspense going, thinking that the opposition will get rattled."By not proroguing the Monsoon Session, the self-styled Chanakya may think he is playing mind games and indulging in psy-ops. But this is silly since the govt can convene a session any time it wants to for any purpose. He is just keeping the suspense going, thinking that the opposition will get rattled. He can continue to hallucinate," Jairam Ramesh said."Why is the Modi govt refusing to convene an All-Party meeting to discuss its proposals for delimitation so as to build the broadest possible consensus - which is what the country needs? This has been the consistent demand of all opposition Parties since mid-March 2026. Why this secrecy and mystery on a subject that is of profound importance to the very fundamentals of the Indian Republic?" he questioned.This comes as Congress has been questioning the delay in proroguing Parliament's Monsoon session, saying "something fishy" was going on and the government was trying to conjure up a "super-tainted" two-thirds majority, but it would not succeed in achieving that.During the Budget session on April 17, the Modi government faced a setback as the Constitution amendment bill, involving delimitation, for the implementation of the women's reservation in the Lok Sabha and state assemblies was defeated in the Lower House.Of the 528 MPs who voted, 298 voted in support, while 230 opposed it. The bill required 352 votes for a two-thirds majority.
Article Summary: The gap between the adjournment of Parliament sine die and its prorogation has reached 29 days. The gap for the 2015 Monsoon Session was 28 days. Congress leader Jairam Ramesh said the government is keeping the suspense going, thinking the opposition will get rattled.

Article Title: Yogi Adityanath pays tribute to UP's first CM Govind Ballabh Pant on his 139th birth anniversary
Article Text:
Yogi Adityanath pays tribute to UP's first CM Govind Ballabh Pant on his 139th birth anniversary

Uttar Pradesh chief minister Yogi Adityanath on Thursday paid floral tribute to the state's first chief minister and freedom fighter Pandit Govind Ballabh Pant on his 139th birth anniversary, recalling his contributions to India's freedom struggle, governance and social reforms.Speaking at an event held to mark the birth anniversary, Yogi Adityanath described Pant as a great advocate and freedom fighter who played a significant role in the country's struggle for independence."On this occasion, on behalf of the Government of Uttar Pradesh and the revered people of Uttar Pradesh, I pay homage to the memories of Pandit Govind Ballabh Pant ji on the occasion of his auspicious birth anniversary, and offer my humble tributes," Yogi said.Recalling Pant's contribution to the Kakori case, the chief minister said that in 1925, Pant had strongly defended revolutionaries facing a case filed by the British government following the Kakori Train Action.He said Pant actively participated in the freedom movement and resigned as the Premier of Uttar Pradesh after being elected to the post in 1937, choosing instead to join the struggle against British rule."Whether it was the Quit India Movement or other major agitations from time to time for the freedom struggle, he actively took part in them," Yogi said.The Chief Minister highlighted Pant's role after Independence, saying he became the first chief minister of Uttar Pradesh in 1947, when present-day Uttarakhand was also part of the state."As the first chief minister of Uttar Pradesh... he initiated efforts to present the governance of such a large state as a model of good governance, foster its economic development, and work for the welfare of every section of society," he said.Yogi also recalled Pant's contribution to land reforms and described the model introduced during his tenure as exemplary.Later, as Union Home minister from 1954, Pant worked to address linguistic conflicts and played an important role in establishing Hindi as the official language, Yogi said."On this occasion, on behalf of the Government of Uttar Pradesh and the people of Uttar Pradesh, I pay homage to his memory and offer my humble tributes to him," the chief minister said.
Article Summary: Yogi Adityanath pays tribute to UP's first CM Govind Ballabh Pant on his 139th birth anniversary. Yogi described Pant as a great advocate and freedom fighter who played a significant role in the country's struggle for independence.

Article Title: BJP national president Nitin Nabin, Uttarakhand CM Pushkar Singh Dhami interact with youth in Haldwani
Article Text:
Uttarakhand CM Pushkar Singh Dhami and BJP national president Nitin Nabin interact with youth in Haldwani, Uttarakhand, on September 20, 2026.

Nabin cites central schemes, emerging opportunities

Dhami highlights recruitment, self-employment

Sports infrastructure, technology and investment

HALDWANI: BJP national president Nitin Nabin and Uttarakhand chief minister Pushkar Singh Dhami took part in a youth interaction programme in Haldwani, where they discussed careers, employment, entrepreneurship, skill development, technology, sports and the future of Uttarakhand with young participants.During the interaction, participants raised questions related to the development of the state and the country. They also shared their experiences of various government schemes and offered suggestions on employment, self-employment and access to better opportunities in Uttarakhand.Nabin said that under Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s leadership, the potential of India’s youth was being given a new direction while new opportunities were being created for them. He said initiatives such as Digital India, Startup India, Skill India, Make in India and Khelo India had provided young people with platforms to advance according to their talent, capabilities and skills. He added that young people were not merely seeking employment but were also emerging as creators of jobs and new opportunities.He said the role of youth was increasing amid a rapidly changing economy and advances in technology.According to him, new avenues had opened up in areas such as artificial intelligence, startups, innovation, digital technology and entrepreneurship. He said Uttarakhand’s young people had immense talent and potential and that connecting their energy and capabilities with the state’s development could help take Uttarakhand to new heights.He said that in a mountainous state such as Uttarakhand, it was important to expand opportunities in local employment, self-employment, tourism, skill development and entrepreneurship. He added that the ideas, suggestions and aspirations of young people could play an important role in determining the future direction of the state. He called on the youth to turn future challenges into opportunities and actively contribute to building a developed India.He also described social media as a powerful medium and said young people should use it positively for the development of society and the country. He said all 1.4 billion citizens would need to work together to realise the vision of a developed India. He also urged young people to enter politics and public life and contribute to nation-building. He stressed the importance of time management, saying effective use of time was essential for success.Dhami described young people as the country’s greatest strength and said India’s large youth population was providing the nation with new energy, fresh ideas and capabilities. He said the growing use of technology and innovation was also opening up new opportunities for young people.The chief minister said that after assuming office on July 4, 2021, his government began working with the resolve that “the youth and water of the mountains should both serve Uttarakhand.” He said recruitment to vacant posts in government departments was accelerated and that around 34,000 young people had so far been appointed to government services. He also referred to action against irregularities in recruitment examinations, saying members of cheating rackets had been sent to jail and that a crackdown had been launched against those attempting to jeopardize the future of young people.He said the government was not limiting opportunities to government jobs and was also focusing on self-employment, startups and entrepreneurship. He cited the Chief Minister’s Self-Employment Scheme, skill development programmes, homestays and the Chief Minister’s Udyaman Khiladi Scheme as initiatives through which young people were being provided opportunities.The chief minister said Uttarakhand was establishing a new identity in sports and that sports infrastructure was being expanded across the state. He referred to work towards setting up a Sports University in Haldwani and a women’s Sports College in Lohaghat. He also cited Uttarakhand athletes winning more than 100 medals at the National Games, describing it as evidence of the state’s growing sporting talent and changing sports environment.He said opportunities were being created for young people in tourism, local products, science, innovation, artificial intelligence, robotics and other emerging technologies. He also referred to the Investors Summit, saying it had been organized with the objective of generating new investment and employment opportunities, while efforts were under way to expand industrial activity in the mountainous regions of the state.The chief minister said the government was also providing free coaching facilities to young people preparing for competitive examinations to help ensure equal opportunities. He added that the talent, hard work and potential of Uttarakhand’s youth were among the state’s greatest strengths in its effort to build a developed Uttarakhand.BJP state president Mahendra Bhatt, MP Ajay Bhatt, public representatives, party office-bearers and a large number of young people were present at the programme.
Article Summary: BJP national president Nitin Nabin and Uttarakhand chief minister Pushkar Singh Dhami took part in a youth interaction programme in Haldwani. They discussed careers, employment, entrepreneurship, skill development, technology, sports and the future of the state.

NEW DELHI: The battle for Delhi University Students’ Union (DUSU) is taking shape around an issue that extends beyond the campus gates — where and how thousands of students live — as ABVP filed nominations of seven probable candidates on Thursday and intensified its outreach ahead of the polls.Alok Attri, Ishu Maurya, Lakshya Raj Singh, Nitin Tanwar, Riya Chhawari, Tanya Mavi and Yash Dabas filed nominations, with ABVP set to pick four of them for president, vice-president, secretary and joint secretary after scrutiny.ABVP enters the election defending three of the four central posts it won last year — president, secretary and joint secretary — while NSUI holds the vice-president’s post.But the Satya Niketan PG building tragedy has brought student housing and safety sharply into the election discourse, with rival organisations competing over an issue affecting a large section of DU students dependent on private accommodation.ABVP, which has held protests over the incident, has begun a PG-to-PG survey under its “Aakhir Kab Tak?” campaign to identify fire, structural and basic-facility gaps. It is demanding more affordable university hostels, faster construction of new hostels and stricter safety enforcement in PGs and rented accommodation.The issue, however, is not ABVP’s alone. It is also pitching the outgoing DUSU’s record, including CCTV cameras, internships, U-Bus services and Pink Booths.ABVP Delhi secretary Sarthak Sharma said the aim was a union that remained “accessible, accountable and responsive throughout the year”.This version gives the report a campus-wide election story rather than an ABVP press-release frame. Article Title: ED raids Ramnandi Hotels in alleged Rs 132-crore bank fraud case; 9 locations searched
Article Text:

NEW DELHI: The Enforcement Directorate (ED) on Friday conducted searches at nine locations in Bihar, Haryana and Delhi in connection with an alleged bank fraud involving Ramnandi Hotels and Resorts Ltd (RHRL), Gaya. The searches were carried out under Section 17 of the Prevention of Money Laundering Act (PMLA) at six locations in Gaya, two in Gurugram and one in New Delhi, officials said.RHRL is controlled by Akhouri Gopal and his sons, Nishant and Nitesh, according to officials. The ED action follows an investigation into the alleged diversion of loan funds and suspected attempts to move properties to prevent possible attachment.During the probe, the agency found that RHRL allegedly diverted Rs 58 crore out of the Rs 85 crore disbursed by a consortium of banks led by Central Bank of India. The loans were allegedly obtained on the basis of fake or forged project completion reports provided by the company's chartered accountant.The loan facilities were also backed by personal guarantees from Akhouri Gopal and his family members, officials said.The investigation has also flagged five properties that had been pledged or mortgaged with Tata Motors Ltd against outstanding dues of a related group entity. The properties were allegedly sold recently despite being pledged.According to the ED, the properties were sold at grossly undervalued prices, with the sale deeds showing the consideration as cash receipts. Some of the buyers are suspected to be benamis or proxies of Akhouri Gopal, officials said.The agency suspects the transactions were aimed at alienating the properties and preventing coercive action. Some of the buyers were reportedly people of modest means who may not have had the financial capacity to arrange the amounts involved in the transactions.The proceeds of crime in the case, based on the CBI chargesheet, are estimated at around Rs 131.79 crore, corresponding to the non-performing asset (NPA) value, officials said.The searches are part of the ED's ongoing investigation into the alleged bank fraud and related movement of assets.
Article Summary: The Enforcement Directorate (ED) conducted searches at nine locations in Bihar, Haryana and Delhi in connection with an alleged bank fraud. The searches were carried out under Section 17 of the Prevention of Money Laundering Act (PMLA) Some of the buyers are suspected to be benamis or proxies of Akhouri Gopal.

Article Title: Brics Summit 2026: Putin to land in Delhi in few hours; Xi arriving Saturday - top developments
Article Text:
India is set to host the two-day BRICS summit in New Delhi, bringing together global leaders while showcasing the country’s cultural heritage.

Key leaders in India

Key agenda, topics in focus

'All set': PM Modi

Schedule

1,200-1,300 journalists expected

Cultural showcase

Delhi all decked up with beefed up security

India chairs Brics for the fourth time

NEW DELHI: Russian foreign minister Sergey Lavrov arrived in India ahead of the BRICS Summit 2026.Russian President Vladimir Putin is also scheduled to arrive in India later tonight.The 18th Brics Leaders’ Summit will be held in New Delhi on September 12-13, bringing together leaders of the expanded grouping for discussions on economic cooperation, technology, energy and food security, global governance and major geopolitical issues. Prime Minister Narendra Modi will host the summit at Bharat Mandapam as India concludes its year-long Brics chairship and hold key meetings with Putin, Xi jinping and various other leaders.The summit comes amid looming concerns over Russia-Ukraine war, Middle East crisis, Strait of Hormuz shipping and continuing global trade tensions. Leaders are expected to work towards a New Delhi Declaration, while the two-day programme will also include bilateral meetings, an exhibition visit, a gala dinner and cultural events.Russian President Vladimir Putin, Chinese President Xi Jinping, Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian, South African President Cyril Ramaphosa and Indonesian President Prabowo Subianto are among the key leaders expected in New Delhi.UN Secretary-General Antonio Guterres will also attend. PM Modi is scheduled to hold bilateral meetings with several leaders on the sidelines of the summit. His meeting with Putin on Friday comes after their recent talks at the SCO summit, while his engagement with Pezeshkian will take place against the backdrop of the Middle East conflict. The Russian president is set to reach in just a few hours with expected time of arrival 1.15am on September 11.The Prime Minister is scheduled to hold bilateral talks with Putin at 3.30 pm and Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian at 6.15 pm on Friday. Then, according to sources cited by PTI, PM's meeting with Xi Jinping is scheduled for 6 pm on Saturday. During the Modi-Xi talks, the two leaders are expected to review the situation along the Line of Actual Control (LAC) and discuss further steps to normalise bilateral ties, including expanding trade and investment, people familiar with the matter said.The China leader is scheduled to reach Infdia at 12.25 pm on Saturday, September 12.Also read: Putin meeting PM Modi on Friday; energy, defence high on agenda Xi’s visit is particularly significant as it will be his first trip to India in seven years. The Chinese president is expected to travel with a large delegation, with sources, cited by Reuers, earlier estimating around 400 officials, more than twice the number that accompanied him in 2019. His visit comes as New Delhi and Beijing work to stabilise ties after years of border tensions.Read more: China confirms Xi Jinping's India visit for Brics summit on September 12-13, first trip in 7 years Meanwhile, foreign ministers of Ethiopia and Burundi, Gedion Timothewos and Edouard Bizimana, have already arrived in New Delhi on Thursday. Later, Brazil minister of foreign affairs Mauro Vieira also reached New Delhi. Country's president Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva will not be coming due to upcoming Brazil elections.Food and energy security, healthcare, disaster resilience and critical supply chains will be among the key areas of discussion.Leaders are also expected to discuss trade, investment, connectivity, cross-border payments, greater use of national currencies, MSME development, digital trade and artificial intelligence.Development finance, climate resilience, expansion of the New Development Bank and reforms of multilateral financial and political institutions are also on the agenda.The Russia-Ukraine war, the Middle East war and concerns over the Strait of Hormuz are expected to feature in discussions on global and regional developments.US tariff policies and wider changes in global trade will provide the broader economic backdrop. Since Brics decisions are consensus-based, differences among members could make negotiations on the joint declaration challenging.New Delhi is gearing up for the two-day summit, with Bharat Mandapam decked up to welcome world leaders.Modi shared a video of the venue on X on Thursday, ending with the message, “India is gearing up for BRICS 2026”. Sharing the video, he wrote: “All set for BRICS 2026!”The video contains visuals of the Bharat Mandapam, the sprawling complex in central Delhi, which has been decked up for the Summit that is being held on September 12-13 under India's chairship.India is hosting the 18th Brics Summit as the grouping's 2026 chair, with leaders of member and partner countries as well as outreach invitees expected to participate.The main leaders’ programme begins on Saturday, September 12.At 2.35 pm, Brics member-country leaders will hold a closed-door session on “Inclusive Global Governance and Strengthening Multilateralism”. At 4.25 pm, leaders will tour the Bharat Innovates Exhibition, followed by a family photograph and joint tree-planting ceremony at 5.05 pm.PM Modi will host a gala dinner at 7.30 pm.Then, on Sunday, September 13, leaders of member countries, partner nations and outreach invitees will begin arriving at 9:55 am. The official group photograph is scheduled for 10.35 am, followed by the main open session at 10:50 am, titled “Resilience, Innovation, Cooperation and Sustainability: Shaping the Future for Inclusive Global Growth”.The summit is expected to conclude with the New Delhi Declaration.The ministry of external affairs expects around 1,200-1,300 journalists to cover the summit, with Indian and foreign media expected to be roughly evenly represented.An International Media Centre is being set up at Bharat Mandapam. The government plans to disseminate information through press releases, websites and social media platforms linked to India’s Brics presidency.Around 160 artistes from India and other Brics countries will perform the “Brics Symphony” at PM Modi’s gala dinner on September 12. The programme will feature Bharatanatyam, Kuchipudi, Odissi and Kathak, along with traditional instruments and vocal performances.A special Brics Friendship Mural is also being created at Bharat Mandapam by artists from member countries, inspired by “Sangam”, or confluence.BRICS banners and posters have gone up across the New Delhi district, while prominent areas including Connaught Place and Khan Market have seen enhanced lighting at night. Security agencies have also stepped up surveillance, with around 500 CCTV cameras deployed across the area, including some equipped with number plate recognition technology.Manish Kumar Agrawal, Special Commissioner of Police (Protective/Security Division), said, "We have made elaborate bandobast by ensuring minimum inconvenience to the public. We have also issued advance advisories regarding traffic arrangements," Agrawal said.Delhi Police has put in place multi-layered security and quick-response arrangements to ensure the movement of visiting leaders and delegates. Senior officers have also been directed to maintain strict vigilance and ensure smooth coordination during the summit.Traffic restrictions are expected in parts of the city during the movement of foreign dignitaries, which could affect commuters despite markets and commercial areas remaining operational.Also read: Going to airport, central Delhi or south Delhi? BRICS traffic restrictions you need to know Connaught Place will remain open from September 11 to 13, although traffic restrictions linked to the summit may affect movement.The Delhi Metro Museum at Supreme Court Metro station will remain closed from September 11 to 13 and reopen on September 15.Rashtrapati Bhavan, the Rashtrapati Bhavan Museum and Amrit Udyan will also remain closed to the public from September 11 to 13. The Change of Guard ceremony scheduled for September 12 will not take place.Also read: Brics Summit, nationwide bank strike tomorrow: Are banks open or shut on September 11? Check details Northern Railway has also made temporary changes to train operations from September 11 to 13. Several trains from New Delhi and nearby stations have been cancelled, diverted, rescheduled or short-terminated/originated during the period. Passengers have been advised to check the National Train Enquiry System (NTES) or call 139 for the latest updates before travelling.Read more: Operations at New Delhi railway station to be regulated; several trains cancelled, diverted - check full list Meanwhile, Delhi is likely to witness rain on both days, with the IMD forecasting light to moderate rainfall in parts of the city, even as temperatures remained above normal on Thursday.India assumed the Brics chairship on January 1, 2026, for the fourth time, after previous chairships in 2012, 2016 and 2021.India’s theme for the year is “Building for Resilience, Innovation, Cooperation and Sustainability”, with “Humanity First” as its people-centric approach. During its chairship, India has held more than 350 meetings and high-level engagements across more than 25 cities.Brics originally comprised Brazil, Russia, India, China and South Africa. Egypt, Ethiopia, Iran, the UAE and Saudi Arabia joined in 2024, while Indonesia became a member in 2025.Ten countries, including Belarus, Bolivia, Kazakhstan, Cuba, Malaysia, Nigeria, Thailand, Uganda, Uzbekistan and Vietnam, have joined as partner countries.The 11-member grouping accounts for about 49.5 per cent of the world's population, around 40 per cent of global GDP and about 26 per cent of global trade, according to Indian government figures.
Article Summary: Russian President Vladimir Putin, Chinese President Xi Jinping, Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian, South African President Cyril Ramaphosa and Indonesian President Prabowo Subianto are among the key leaders expected in New Delhi. PM Modi is scheduled to hold bilateral meetings with several leaders on the sidelines of the summit.

Article Title: Modi-Xi meet: Trade, border on agenda during Xi's 24-hour blitz
Article Text:
Xi Jinping to visit India after 7 years, attend BRICS Summit on Sept 12-13

China announced Thursday President Xi Jinping ’s first visit to India in 7 years, saying he will attend the Brics summit in New Delhi from September 12 to 13 at the invitation of PM Narendra Modi. His bilateral with Modi is scheduled for Saturday evening, according to diplomatic sources.TOI has learnt that Xi will be accompanied by a 67-member government delegation, including political heavyweight and Xi’s right-hand man Cai Qi - member of the standing committee of the CPC Politburo - and foreign minister Wang Yi. A business delegation is arriving separately for the president’s visit that will last exactly for 24 hours, beginning with Xi’s arrival at 12.10 pm on Saturday and 12.20 pm departure the next day.Xi will arrive at Bharat Mandapam around 2 pm on Saturday, where he and other leaders will be welcomed by Modi. The bilateral meeting between the leaders is likely to take place between the Brics closed session on multilateralism and the dinner that Modi will host for the leaders at 7.30 pm in which Xi will also be present.There has been speculation about why Beijing delayed the announcement of the visit, but it’s learnt that China had formally conveyed to the Indian side Xi’s participation weeks earlier.On August 27, China officially requested the Indian embassy in Beijing to issue visas to the president’s delegation.Xi’s visit is expected to reinforce the positive momentum in bilateral ties since the meeting between the leaders on the margins of the BRICS summit in Kazan in 2024, which marked complete disengagement and resolution of issues related to the 2020 eastern Ladakh military standoff. Modi is expected to underline India’s concerns about fair market access, supply chain reliability and balance in bilateral trade in the meeting, as the 2 sides look to boost economic cooperation.The leaders had in Kazan agreed to restart high-level engagements, calling upon Special Representatives on the India-China boundary question to oversee the management of peace and tranquility in border areas, which India calls a prerequisite for overall development of ties, and to explore a fair, reasonable and mutually acceptable solution to the boundary question. They also agreed to maintain contact at the level of foreign minister and other senior officials.Since then, the special representatives have thrice held boundary talks, with the latest meeting in August this year resulting in 8 outcomes that included a decision to finalise terms of reference for an early and substantial harvest of boundary delimitation and border management.Modi last year also visited China for the SCO summit, during which he also had a bilateral meeting with Xi. That visit too further solidified the thaw in ties, with both leaders agreeing that India and China are partners, not rivals. Xi’s visit is important for Beijing also as China assumes BRICS presidency next year, succeeding India’s chairship. The president had not travelled to Brazil last year for the BRICS summit.During his visit to Tianjin, Modi had also met Cai and shared his vision for bilateral relations and seeking his support to realise the vision of the two leaders. According to the Indian government, Cai had reiterated the Chinese sides desire to expand bilateral exchanges and further improve relations in line with the consensus reached between the two leaders.
Article Summary: Xi Jinping to visit India after 7 years, attend BRICS Summit on Sept 12-13. His bilateral with Modi is scheduled for Saturday evening, according to diplomatic sources. Xi’s visit is important for Beijing also as China assumes BRICS presidency next year.

Article Title: Russia President Vladimir Putin arrives in India ahead of Brics Summit 2026, to meet PM Modi
Article Text:
PM Modi to meet Putin later in the day

NEW DELHI: Russian President Vladimir Putin arrived in India on early Friday ahead of the Brics Summit 2026.Russian president's official air vehicle landed at Delhi airport.During his visit, Putin is scheduled to hold talks with Prime Minister Narendra Modi and participate in a series of bilateral meetings.This mark his first overseas participation in a Brics Summit since Russia invaded Ukraine in February 2022.The two leaders are expected to discuss the full range of India-Russia ties, with trade, energy and defence cooperation likely to figure prominently.The visit comes just days after PM Modi and Putin met on the sidelines of the Shanghai Cooperation Organisation summit in Bishkek on August 31. At that meeting, the two leaders reviewed cooperation in areas including political ties, trade, defence, energy, space and mobility, while also discussing the conflicts in West Asia and the Black Sea region.Putin’s presence in Delhi also comes as India and Russia seek to deepen economic engagement despite mounting geopolitical pressure over Moscow’s war in Ukraine and Western restrictions on Russian trade.Russian presidential spokesperson Dmitry Peskov had earlier said the two sides are also exploring cooperation in rare earths, along with the possible sale of Sukhoi Su-57 stealth fighter jets to India.Speaking to reporters during a virtual briefing from Moscow, Peskov said, "We're looking forward to the President and Prime Minister having another bilateral meeting during the visit.It is scheduled. It is scheduled for Friday, so first, like always, they will touch on the bilateral agenda. Trade and economic cooperation is a very wide scope."On the agenda during Putin’s visit for the summit is also the possible sale of Russia’s Su-57 stealth fighters to India.Union civil aviation minister Kinjarapu Ram Mohan Naidu confirmed on Thursday that India and Russia have stepped up talks on manufacturing aircraft in India, including the IL-114 turboprop and Sukhoi Superjet 100.
Article Summary: Russian President Vladimir Putin arrived in India on early Friday ahead of the Brics Summit 2026. Putin is scheduled to hold talks with Prime Minister Narendra Modi and participate in a series of bilateral meetings. Visit comes just days after PM Modi and Putin met on the sidelines of the Shanghai Cooperation Organisation summit in Bishkek.

Article Title: Tamil Nadu govt tells staff to file annual asset declarations online by October
Article Text:

CHENNAI: Tamil Nadu govt has made it mandatory for all govt employees, barring All India Service officers, to submit their annual statements of assets and liabilities online through the Integrated Financial and Human Resources Management System (IFHRMS).The move follows an amendment to Rule 7(3) of Tamil Nadu Government Servants’ Conduct Rules made in Jan 2026 by the DMK regime. Employees are required to declare their immovable properties, including land and buildings, movable assets such as vehicles, jewellery and bank deposits, as well as debts and other liabilities through the IFHRMS portal. “The facility for filing details of assets and liabilities has now been enabled on the IFHRMS portal. The system will make it easier to monitor violations,,” a senior official said.In a recent communication, the govt directed secretaries, heads of departments, district collectors, judges, TNPSC secretary and registrar of Madras high court to instruct employees to file statements for the calendar year ending Dec 31, 2025, by Oct 31, 2026.The date of filing will be recorded in an employee’s ‘annual confidential report’.Failure to submit the statement within the stipulated period will be treated as a violation of the service conduct rules.Employees must file statements of their assets and liabilities as on Dec 31 of each year by March 31 of the succeeding year. The govt has also advised employees to keep their IFHRMS user IDs and passwords secure. Employees have to use Form I for immovable property, Form II for movable property and Form III for debts and other liabilities. After verifying and correcting the details, they must confirm and submit the declaration and download a copy for their records.“Not many employees take the declaration seriously. Submission of the statement will be considered during panel preparation for promotion. Making it mandatory is a welcome step as it would help prevent corruption at all levels,” said a member of Jactto-Geo, an umbrella federation of govt employees.In July, the TVK govt introduced a WhatsApp number — 9498180936 — for reporting instances of govt employees demanding bribes. Heads of departments were directed to ensure that anti-bribery notice boards were prominently displayed in govt offices and public places.
Article Summary: The move follows an amendment to Rule 7(3) of Tamil Nadu Government Servants’ Conduct Rules made in Jan 2026 by the DMK regime. Employees are required to declare their immovable properties, including land and buildings, movable assets such as vehicles, jewellery and bank deposits.

Article Title: 2.5 lakh crore spent on disaster management in 11 years: Amit Shah
Article Text: NEW DELHI: Around Rs 2.5 lakh crore has been spent in the disaster management sector over the last 11 years, increasing allocations for national and state disaster response funds manifold, home minister Amit Shah said while chairing the third meeting of the governing body of National Institute of Disaster Management (NIDM) Thursday.Shah said the process of creating digital disaster databases at national and state levels has begun, an obligation for all UN member states as decided in Sendai framework in 2015. Article Title: Global climate record: August this year joint-warmest month with July '23
Article Text:
Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Aug 2026 was the joint-warmest month ever recorded globally across all calendar months, on a par with July 2023, said Copernicus Climate Change Service (C3S) of the European Union's space programme on Thursday.It noted that this Aug was 1.65° Celsius above the estimated pre-industrial (1850-1900) baseline, marking the first month above 1.5° Celsius since Nov 2025, and the period from June to Aug 2026 was the joint-warmest three-month period on record globally, on a par with 2024."Aug 2026 was a remarkable month in the global climate record. It was both the warmest Aug and the warmest month ever recorded," said Samantha Burgess, strategic lead for climate at European Centre for Medium-Range Weather Forecasts. Though the global average temperature rise in the month breached the limit of 1.5°C, it technically did not cross the Paris Agreement threshold, which actually refers to long-term temperature increase over decades, not over one to five years.Under the Paris Agreement, countries agreed to keep long-term global average surface temperature well below 2°C above pre-industrial levels and pursue efforts to limit it to 1.5°C by end of century.Nevertheless, the rise in temperatures to this level in Aug is a stark warning that the world is getting warmer, with its consequences of extreme weather events, glacier melt, sea-level rise and uneven distribution of rainfall over a short period of time being visible across the globe."Until humanity stops burning colossal amount of coal, oil and gas, the pollution this causes will keep baking our planet, and extreme heat will keep smashing all-time records, killing millions and costing trillions, hitting transport and health systems, and pushing up prices for household basics like food," said UN Climate Change executive secretary Simon Stiell in his response to the report.Aug in India was the warmest Aug in the country since 1901, with a mean monthly temperature of 28.01°C.
Article Summary: Aug 2026 was the joint-warmest month ever recorded globally across all calendar months. This Aug was 1.65° Celsius above the estimated pre-industrial (1850-1900) baseline. It was the first month above 1.5° Celsius since Nov 2025.

Article Title: SC junks anti-HPV vax PIL, says plea has ulterior motive
Article Text: NEW DELHI: Supreme Court Thursday dismissed a PIL by a doctors' association challenging India's nationwide human papillomavirus (HPV) vaccination programme for adolescent girls to protect them against cervical cancer and said it did not behove medical practitioners to take an anti-vaccine stance.Though the NGO's counsel clarified at the outset that the PIL was not against the vaccination programme but for putting in place mechanisms to take care of adverse reactions and compensation, a bench led by CJI Surya Kant said, "The PIL is definitely anti-vaccine." It gave the option to the lawyer to withdraw or invite adverse comments.When the counsel continued to argue for prior informed consent of parents of the target population of adolescent girls, the bench said the PIL appeared to have been filed with an ulterior motive and lacked bona fide. It said when there was an established mechanism for taking care of adverse reactions and compensation in individual cases, it did not behove doctors to oppose vaccination when World Health Organisation had recommended it.The NGO said eminent oncologists have pointed to data that shows cervical cancer incidence has declined over the past three decades.
Article Summary: Supreme Court dismisses a PIL by a doctors' association challenging India's vaccination programme for adolescent girls to protect them against cervical cancer. Article Title: Checks on e-commerce platforms from October: FSSAI
Article Text:

New Delhi: Having secured nearly 2,000 convictions in food safety cases across the country, Food Safety and Standards Authority of India (FSSAI) is now stepping up enforcement, including holding e-commerce platforms responsible for products sold through them and proposing stricter action against high-fat, sugar and salt (HFSS) foods near schools, its CEO Rajit Punhani said Thursday.FSSAI will begin checks on e-commerce platforms from next month. Platforms will have to carry out due diligence and ensure that products listed on them comply with food safety regulations."We are holding e-commerce platforms responsible. They cannot take this plea that they are just aggregators, they are just platforms. It is your responsibility, your due diligence," Punhani said.FSSAI has already held consultations with e-commerce companies. Punhani identified e-commerce and labelling as two major consumer-focused reforms expected over the next year.The regulator has also proposed restricting the sale of HFSS food within 50 metres of schools to protect children from unhealthy food. Punhani said the earlier challenge was the absence of a clear definition of HFSS food. The Indian Council of Medical Research-National Institute of Nutrition, a govt nutrition research institute, has now provided criteria that FSSAI plans to use.On enforcement, Punhani said FSSAI had suspended licences, closed establishments and launched prosecutions. Around 600 people had been arrested in criminal cases involving unsafe food in the previous six months, he said. He cited around 1,900 convictions and 33,000 notices issued across India for food safety violations, including adulteration, mislabelling and substandard food.FSSAI is also tightening rules on food claims and marketing. It does not allow "100%" claims except in cases under litigation, while "pure" and "natural" can be used only for single-ingredient products, provided nothing has been added. The regulator has also written to Department for Promotion of Industry and Internal Trade and the Controller General of Patents, Designs and Trade Marks over the use of "healthy" as a trademark.Punhani said the term "energy drink" would not be allowed on labels as it could mislead consumers, with such products classified as caffeinated beverages, while the proposed red warning system would also cover aerated, carbonated and caffeinated beverages. The regulator has issued notices to six celebrities over misleading food-related endorsements, with three having responded.
Article Summary: Food Safety and Standards Authority of India (FSSAI) will begin checks on e-commerce platforms from next month. The regulator has also proposed restricting the sale of HFSS food within 50 metres of schools. FSSAI is also tightening rules on food claims and marketing.

Article Title: Need social media firewalls, safeguards for minors: Supreme Court
Article Text:

NEW DELHI: With minors' access to social media platforms banned in many countries, Supreme Court Thursday took the first step in this regard by seeking govt's response to a PIL that said opening a social media account is akin to signing a contract - which is impermissible for a person below 18 years of age under Indian law.The plea by senior advocate H S Phoolka, on behalf of NGO Just Rights for Children Association, found resonance with a bench of CJI Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana, which said there was a need for safeguards and firewalls to protect minors.Phoolka said children were at present permitted to independently create and maintain accounts on social media platforms and access digital platforms "notwithstanding their statutory incapacity to enter into a contract under Section 11 of Indian Contract Act, 1872", and said such contracts are void ab initio.The NGO said the absence of an effective and uniform mechanism giving practical effect to such statutory incapacity in the digital environment exposed children to "foreseeable risks, including online grooming, sexual exploitation, trafficking, behavioural profiling, misuse of personal data, cyberbullying, exposure to age-inappropriate content and other harms affecting their safety, dignity, development and well-being".It requested the court to direct govt to ensure that persons below 18 years of age are not permitted to enter into contracts with digital platforms, including social media, online gaming, content-sharing, live-streaming and other user generated content platforms. It said minors could be permitted to access lawful, educational and age-appropriate digital content through accounts maintained and controlled by their parents or guardians, subject to an appropriate regulatory framework.Phoolka said social media platforms applied US law in India, not Indian law. In US, a person above 13 years can lawfully enter into a contract. CJI Kant said, "We need some safeguards in India." Justice Bagchi said, "There should be some firewalls."The NGO said opening of accounts includes acceptance of contractual terms and conditions, user agreements, privacy policy, etc, which govern the relationship between the platform and the user.Referring to provisions of Digital Personal Data Protection Act, the NGO said Section 9 required verifiable parental or guardian consent for processing a child's personal data. The Act also imposes restrictions concerning detrimental processing, tracking, behavioural monitoring and targeted advertising, it said.However, the existing statutory framework does not expressly prohibit a person below 18 from independently creating an account on a digital platform nor does it prescribe a uniform mechanism for preventing such independent opening of accounts, it said.
Article Summary: Supreme Court seeks govt's response to a PIL that said opening a social media account is akin to signing a contract. The plea by senior advocate H S Phoolka found resonance with a bench of CJI Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana.

Article Title: Chandrayaan-2 orbiter is still alive and helping in subsequent future lunar missions: Sr Indian scientist
Article Text:

NEW DELHI: A senior Indian space scientist on Thursday said that the orbiter of the Chandrayaan-2 mission, which was said to be a failed mission after its lander crashlanded on the south pole region of Moon, is still alive and is helping in planning and executing subsequent Indian lunar missions.During the AEDEX conference at Yashobhoomi here on Thursday, Anil Bhardwaj, director of Ahmedabad-based Physical Research Laboratory (PRL) under the Department of Space, said, “It was the Chandrayaan-2 orbiter that provided crucial information to Isro about where to land the Chandrayaan-3 lander.”Chandrayaan-2 orbiter, which was launched in 2019, is currently operating from the Moon’s orbit. “It has the highest resolution among all the assets in the world operating on the Moon. It is now being used for future missions,” Bhardwaj said.Chandrayaan-2 orbiter carried eight scientific payloads designed to study the lunar surface, minerals, and exosphere. The orbiter is equipped with the Orbiter High Resolution Camera (OHRC), which features a spatial resolution of about 0.25 meters (25 cm) to 0.32 meters per pixel from a 100-kilometer lunar orbit.“For Chandrayaan-4, we have built sensors that will help in landing and bringing back lunar samples back to Earth,” the PRL director said.“Chandrayaan-5 will be a joint mission with Japan agency JAXA, where the lander will try to land in the permanently-shadowed region of the Moon. This region is near the south pole of the Moon and it never sees the sunlight. This will be a very challenging mission. The rover will go inside the permanently-shadowed region and explore for the first time the area. There again we are trying to put up very unique sensors to provide us information about the distribution of water.So sensor development is happening at a speedy level.”“India is also working on hi-tech sensors for in-situ (natural place) experiments,” Bhardwaj said. He also said the work is on in developing a heating system so that the lander can survive freezing temperatures during the 14 Earth nights (one lunar night is equal to 14 Earth days).
Article Summary: Chandrayaan-2 orbiter, which was launched in 2019, is currently operating from the Moon’s orbit. “It has the highest resolution among all the assets in the world operating on the Moon. It is now being used for future missions,” Anil Bhardwaj said.

Article Title: SC asks Centre to reduce cut-off to prevent super-specialty med seats going waste

CHENNAI/NEW DELHI: As about 1,800 of the more than 4,000 super-specialty medical seats are lying vacant even after two rounds of counselling, Supreme Court on Thursday asked the Union govt to consider lowering the NEET-SS 2025 qualifying cutoff marks.“Having examined the matter from different perspectives, we are of the opinion that it may be necessary to reconsider the decision for reducing the cut-off percentile,” a bench of Justice Pamidighantam Sri Narasimha and Justice Alok Aradhe said.“This is rather compelling because a large number of seats have remained unfilled even as of today,” the court said in the case concerning admissions under NEET-SS 2025 counselling.The bench asked additional solicitor-general Aishwarya Bhati to convey its concern to the Union health ministry and seek an appropriate decision and listed the matter for Sept 17.Earlier, Centre told Supreme Court that it had decided not to reduce the cut-off marks this year after consultations between all stakeholders — ministry of health, medical counselling committee (MCC) and National Medical Commission (NMC).“As per the directions of Supreme Court in the Kevin Joy case (2023), it has been decided to conduct a ‘special stray round’ by the medical counselling committee for the purpose of filling the vacant super-specialty seats arising out of NEET-SS 2025 counselling without reduction in the percentile criteria prescribed for admission in the said special stray round,” Bhati said, placing before the court a one-page note on the govt’s decision.Advocate Rashmi Nandakumar, appearing for some of the petitioners, however, told the bench that around 2,000 seats in colleges would remain vacant if the cut-off percentile was not reduced. She said that in the past, authorities had conducted special rounds, mop-up rounds, stray vacancy rounds and relaxation of eligibility criteria, whenever substantial super-specialty seats remained vacant. She said that at least a mop-up/stray vacancy round be conducted for seats remaining vacant after completion of the ongoing counselling process so that no super-specialty seat would go waste.Senior counsel P Wilson, who appeared on behalf of service doctors in Tamil Nadu, told the court that the 1,800 super-specialty seats remaining vacant included cardiology, neurosurgery and oncology — disciplines that train doctors to manage some of the country’s most complex illnesses. Allowing such seats to lapse would waste public investment and deepen the shortage of trained specialists, he said.Doctors told TOI that they were tired of waiting for admissions. The eligibility test for super-specialty admissions was completed in Dec 2025, and results were announced a month later. Until now, two rounds of counselling have been completed, and more than 1,800 seats, including those in cardiology, cardiothoracic surgery, neurosurgery, and haematology, are vacant. “How can so many doctors, physicians and surgeons, be kept on wait for such a long time?” asked Dr R Sathish, a physician.“Unlike in MBBS or sometimes PGs, most candidates are breadwinners. Admissions to a super-specialty course means training while working for a hospital. Many have quit jobs in Feb waiting for admissions. While the seat we want is vacant, we don’t get it,” he said.Experts said that in earlier years, the authorities reduced the qualifying cutoff to zero after regular counselling rounds. “That made doctors who had appeared for the examination eligible to compete for vacant seats. Those single digits, zero or negative marks, become eligible,” said Dr K Senthil, former member of the postgraduate board of National Medical Commission. This relaxation offers an immediate way to prevent seats from going unused, without addressing broader issues such as weak job prospects after training, modest salaries, demanding work conditions and uncertain career paths, he said.
Article Summary: About 1,800 of the more than 4,000 super-specialty medical seats are lying vacant. Supreme Court on Thursday asked the Union govt to consider lowering the NEET-SS 2025 qualifying cutoff marks. Centre told Supreme Court that it had decided not to reduce the cut-off marks this year.

NEW DELHI: PM Narendra Modi, at the International Space Summit in Paris, on Thursday hailed Isro and its scientists, called for global cooperation in the sector and said his country “supports a safe, secure and sustainable space domain anchored in international law”.Addressing the summit virtually from Delhi, Modi said, “India’s approach is rooted in Vasudhaiva Kutumbakam, that is One Earth, One Family, One Future. This spirit must now travel beyond Earth. India’s space journey reflects this philosophy. Isro, which stands at the heart of this journey, has earned global admiration for its excellence and cost-effective missions. Its capabilities serve farmers and fishermen, weather forecasting, disaster management and navigation. More than 430 satellites from 34 countries have travelled to space aboard Indian rockets. Isro’s technologies and partnerships serve not only India, but the wider world.”Praising Isro scientists, the PM said, “Behind this global trust is the dedication and hard work of generations of Indian scientists, engineers and technicians. Working day and night, they have built Isro’s global reputation mission by mission, success by success, and given India a place of pride among spacefaring nations.”Modi’s praise will act as a morale booster for Isro employees, some of whom had recently written to the Isro chief, raising concerns about the “shift towards privatisation”. After nine employee associations had sought written clarification from the Isro chairman on privatisation push, agency head V Narayanan and INSPACe chairman Pawan Goenka had allayed fears of the staff, saying there was no move to privatise the organisation and that reforms were meant to widen the space ecosystem.On the private sector, the PM said, “Alongside Isro, India’s private space sector is also surging in a big way. The energy of enterprise is joining the excellence of Isro.”On India’s achievements, Modi said, “Chandrayan-3 made India the first nation to land near the lunar south pole. Aditya-L1 is unlocking the secrets of the Sun. Last year, an Indian visited the International Space Station. Looking ahead, we aim to establish an Indian space station by 2035 and send an Indian to the Moon by 2040. In all these efforts, our guiding principle has been clear: their benefits must reach all humanity. ”On France's support to India’s space programme, Modi said, “France has been a trusted partner since the Indian space programme began at Thumba in the 1960s. Today, our cooperation spans Earth observation and advanced technologies, uniting scientific excellence with human purpose. We invite France and the world to be co-travellers in India’s next space frontier.”The PM said for centuries, space inspired people's imagination and now, it shapes life on Earth, from climate and crops to oceans and communities. “The promise of space is infinite. Our responsibility is collective. As orbits become more crowded, technologies more powerful, and actors more numerous, our choices must be clear: cooperation over confrontation; sustainability over short-term gain; and inclusion over exclusion," he said.Sending a global message from the summit, Modi said, “We will explore together, innovate together and protect space together, for all humanity, and for generations to come.”

Article Title: Brics turns 25: How a Goldman Sachs acronym became a global power bloc
Article Text:
New Delhi will play host to the 18th Brics Summit

From a Wall Street acronym to a global grouping

Why Brics matters in the changing global order

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

The 18th Brics Summit is set to take place in New Delhi on September 12-13, bringing together leaders of the expanded grouping at a time when wars, trade tensions and a shifting global order are testing its ability to act as a united bloc.India is hosting the summit as the current Brics chair, with the grouping now comprising 11 members and 10 partner countries.Under the theme “Building for Resilience, Innovation, Cooperation and Sustainability,” New Delhi has placed greater focus on cooperation across economic and financial issues, technology, energy, development and global governance.The scale of that transformation becomes clearer when traced back to the origins of Brics, a term coined 25 years ago by a Goldman Sachs economist to describe four emerging economies that he believed would become major drivers of global growth.Twenty-five years ago, Brics did not exist as a political grouping. It was a term coined by Goldman Sachs economist Jim O’Neill in 2001 to describe Brazil, Russia, India and China as emerging economies that could become major drivers of global growth.His paper, Building Better Global Economic BRICs, argued that the weight of these economies in the world economy would rise significantly and called for their greater representation in global policymaking forums.The transition from an economic concept to a government-led grouping began in 2006, when the foreign ministers of Brazil, Russia, India and China met on the sidelines of the UN General Assembly in New York. The first summit of their leaders followed in 2009 in Yekaterinburg, Russia, giving the grouping a formal leaders-level platform.The following year, South Africa joined, turning BRIC into Brics and giving the grouping its first member from Africa.The next major transformation came at the 2023 Johannesburg Summit, when Brics agreed to its first large-scale expansion. Egypt, Ethiopia, Iran, Saudi Arabia and the UAE were invited to join from January 1, 2024. Indonesia subsequently became the bloc's 11th full member in January 2025.The expansion also created a partner-country category, allowing a wider group of developing economies to engage with Brics without becoming full members.Brics has evolved from a forum focused largely on economic cooperation into a broader platform for emerging and developing economies seeking a greater role in global governance.Its members have repeatedly called for reforms in institutions such as the United Nations and international financial institutions, arguing that the architecture of global governance should better reflect the changing balance of economic power.Its growing importance is also backed by institutions created by the grouping itself. The New Development Bank, established in 2015, was designed to mobilise resources for infrastructure and sustainable-development projects in Brics and other emerging and developing economies.The bloc's significance has increased further with its expansion. The addition of countries such as Egypt, Ethiopia, Iran, the UAE and Indonesia has widened Brics' economic and geographic reach and strengthened its claim to be a platform for the Global South.
Article Summary: The 18th Brics Summit is set to take place in New Delhi on September 12-13. India is hosting the summit as the current Brics chair. The grouping now comprises 11 members and 10 partner countries. Brics has evolved from a forum focused on economic cooperation into a broader platform for emerging and developing economies seeking a greater role in global governance.

Article Title: States, municipalities to drive next phase of India deregulation: Niti Aayog member Gauba

MUMBAI: States and municipalities will have to drive the next phase of India’s deregulation, with reforms in areas such as land use, building permits, pollution consents and business licences critical to making it easier to do business, NITI Aayog member Rajiv Gauba said.Speaking at the Global Fintech Fest, Gauba said the next generation of reforms should focus on making the everyday task of doing business simpler, rather than only pursuing large, headline-grabbing measures. He said India needed to move beyond the persistence of the “Inspector Raj” by scrutinising the maze of laws, regulations, permissions, registrations and renewal requirements imposed by governments at the Centre, state and city levels.“The next generation reform has to be to liberate the industry and citizens at large from this stifling chokehold of rules, regulations, permissions,” Gauba said.The approach, he said, should be based on trust, with regulations tested against the principle of “Jan Vishwas”. Licences should be required only for activities involving national security or serious risks to human health or the environment. In other cases, registration should be automatic rather than subject to a government “yes or no”.Where licences are necessary, they should have perpetual or long-term, 10-year validity, while inspections should be risk-based rather than random.Gauba pointed out that several areas that directly affect investment and economic activity, including land-use changes, building permits, pollution consents and various business licences, fall within the jurisdiction of state and municipal governments.The Centre, he said, should promote model regulations, share templates and best practices and create incentives for states to implement them. Central transfers and fiscal support can be linked to reforms, with the Special Assistance Scheme for Capital Investment and the Urban Challenge Fund providing examples of funding being tied to reforms and projects.One major opportunity lies in easing building regulations. Gauba said changes to requirements relating to setbacks, ground coverage and parking could unlock five to six times more built-up area. This could allow hospitals to add floors and hotels to build more rooms, while increasing land supply could help reduce hotel tariffs by 35% and make affordable housing more accessible.Tourism and hospitality also need deregulation, he said. Tour operators currently require various state-level permits despite holding an All India Tourist Permit, while hotels face multiple health, trade and liquor licences across venues and locations. The committee has recommended sweeping reforms in these areas, and the deregulation task force is now working with states to implement them.
Article Summary: NITI Aayog member Rajiv Gauba says states and municipalities will have to drive the next phase of India’s deregulation. Article Title: Space-based surveillance: Dhruva to get key systems worth €5m from Safran

BENGALURU: French firm Safran Space, under contracts worth more than €5 million, will supply critical systems, including optical payloads, for satellites being built as part of India’s Space-Based Surveillance-3 (SBS-3) programme by Dhruva Space, a release from the French President’s Office has confirmed.The contracts, signed during the International Space Summit in Paris, cover communication systems, inertial navigation units, optical payloads and ground stations for the constellation, which is planned to be deployed between 2027 and 2030.SBS-3, a strategic project approved by the Cabinet Committee on Security, will comprise 52 satellites in low Earth and geostationary orbits and is aimed at providing the armed forces with persistent surveillance, secure communications and greater situational awareness across India’s land and maritime areas of interest.The programme marks an expansion of the private sector’s role in India’s strategic space capabilities. Of the 52 satellites, 31 are to be built by private industry, with the remaining 21 being built by Isro. The private-sector allocation has been divided among three companies: Antaris will build 15 satellites, while Pixxel and Dhruva Space will build eight each.Dhruva’s eight satellites therefore form part of the private-sector component of the larger SBS-3 constellation, rather than a separate constellation.The programme is expected to improve the frequency with which strategic areas can be observed and strengthen India’s ability to monitor developments along its borders and across the Indian Ocean Region.The Safran contracts will give Dhruva access to a range of French technologies for the satellites and associated ground infrastructure. Safran said the cooperation illustrates the rise of Indian New Space and the ability of French industry to support the development of India’s sovereign space capabilities. The company also said the partnership could open the way to further cooperation under future phases of the SBS programme.The Paris summit also produced two other India-related announcements. French launch-services provider RIDE! signed an agreement to launch two satellites for TakeMeToSpace, an Indian company developing orbital data centres. The deal builds on RIDE!’s collaboration with Indian space companies, including the launch of a European atmospheric re-entry capsule aboard Isro’s PSLV.Separately, French Earth-observation company U-Space and Indian company Axiscades signed a commercial cooperation agreement to explore the Indian microsatellite market, addressing both commercial and institutional demand.Together, the three announcements point to a widening India-France space relationship spanning strategic surveillance, satellite launches and commercial satellite manufacturing, with Indian private companies increasingly at the centre of the cooperation.

NEW DELHI: The Supreme Court on Thursday sought responses from the Uttar Pradesh government and others on a plea challenging provisions of a 1980 law that provide pension and other facilities to sitting and former MLAs and MLCs in the state.A bench of Justices Vikram Nath and Sandeep Mehta issued notice on the petition challenging a May verdict of the Lucknow bench of the Allahabad High Court, which had dismissed the plea against the constitutional validity of the provisions.The top court posted the matter for hearing after four weeks.The petitioner, Lok Prahari, had challenged provisions of the Uttar Pradesh State Legislature (Members' Emoluments and Pension) Act, 1980, arguing that the state legislature had effectively made itself the “judge in its own cause” by granting benefits to its sitting and former members.The plea contended that the benefits were “manifestly arbitrary” and contrary to the constitutional principle that public office is meant for public service and not personal gain.The High Court had noted that the law provides sitting and former MLAs and MLCs with salary, allowances and other facilities.
