Article Title: Strategic Autonomy in motion as India hosts 18th BRICS Summit
Article Text:
This would be the 18th summit of the grouping. (Photo: ANI)

India for BRICS

Key Challenges for India

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

India will host the annual BRICS summit on September 12-13 at Bharat Mandapam, returning to the venue where it held the G20 summit in 2023. That gathering is remembered for the inclusion of the African Union in G20, marking a major step in efforts to bridge the gap between the Western-led global order and the emerging Global South. At BRICS, India will look to leverage that momentum, working with major emerging economies to demand structural reforms of global governance institutions dominated by the West.This would be the 18th summit of the grouping that brings together 11 major emerging and developing economies – Brazil, Russia, India, China, South Africa, Ethiopia, UAE, Indonesia, Iran, Egypt and Saudi Arabia – along with 10 other partner countries. Together, BRICS nations account for 49 percent of world population, 40 percent of global GDP and 26 percent of international trade.The last time India hosted an in-person BRICS summit was in 2016 in Goa. This year also marks 2 decades of formalisation of the bloc for cooperation on issues related to global economic and political governance. The theme of India's 2026 chairship is Building for Resilience, Innovation, Cooperation and Sustainability, drawing inspiration from PM Narendra Modi's 'humanity first' and people-centric approach to BRICS.This will also be the first summit to see in-person participation by Russian President Vladimir Putin since the start of the Ukraine war. Chinese President Xi Jinping is also visiting India for the first time in 7 years to participate in the summit.Under its chairship, India has so far held over 350 meetings - 25 at the ministerial level including the foreign ministers and national security advisers’ engagements. The ministerial meetings have so far resulted in key outcomes and initiatives spanning agriculture, health, energy, environment, disaster management and also trade, reaffirming commitment to a fair, inclusive and transparent multilateral trading system with WTO at its core.Despite the political fragmentation and economic imbalances associated with the grouping, BRICS remains important for India for multiple reasons, especially in an increasingly uncertain world. For one, it lends India a platform to practice its strategic autonomy and multi-alignment policy, not allowing any one single bloc to acquire excessive leverage over it. That it can simultaneously expand its strategic and technology ties with the West and also work with Quad for a free and open Indo-Pacific reinforces an independent foreign policy. For India, as external affairs minister S Jaishankar has said, BRICS is an embodiment of a multipolar world. India is not giving up on its Western partnerships, only hedging against uncertainty whether from US unpredictability or Chinese ascendancy.BRICS also allows India to showcase its Global South leadership credentials, as it works with other major emerging markets to push for reforms of global institutions like the UNSC, IMF and World Bank that are not representative of the developing world. Support for UNSC reforms is important, although it still falls short of an explicit endorsement of India's permanent membership bid, mainly because of China's presence.India's approach to BRICS is also guided by its complex ties with China. Turning away would mean allowing China to single-handedly shape the agenda of the developing world. BRICS is consensus driven and even for Washington and other Western capitals, India's moderating influence should be of significance as it prevents the bloc from turning into an anti-West platform.There's focus as well on expanding financial architecture as no government would like its trade to be held hostage by instruments it can't control. As Jaishankar has underlined, institutions such as the New Development Bank and the Contingent Reserve Arrangement demonstrate the group's ability to create credible alternatives. For India, these are not initiatives targeted at any currency. In any case, India has officially said it's against de-dollarisation or any attempt to target the US currency. It has also ruled out any proposal for a common BRICS currency.BRICS provides India with markets, along with trade diversification, de-risking and supply-chain opportunities. According to a commerce ministry press release, intra-BRICS merchandise trade reached approximately $1.17 trillion in 2024. India exported an estimated $82 billion in goods to BRICS members in FY2025–26, alongside approximately $31.3 billion in services exports in 2024. BRICS membership deepens India’s trade relationships with Russia (energy), Brazil (agriculture/commodities), Gulf and African countries, diversifying away from overreliance on any single partner.The first of course is to forge a consensus on West Asia that would enable a joint BRICS declaration, a task complicated by the presence of the UAE and Iran in the group. India would not like the event to end with a Chair's Statement, like what happened with the foreign ministers' meeting, knowing well that no BRICS summit has concluded without a comprehensive joint declaration. Foreign secretary Vikram Misri said last week India has received cooperation from all members and the government is working to arrive eventually at a constructive outcome that benefits all BRICS stakeholders. India will focus on drafting a resolution rooted in the UN Charter, dialogue and diplomacy, freedom of navigation and civilian protection, while looking to ringfence economic agreements from contentious political issues by acknowledging respective national positions.Balancing relations with the US is another key concern for India, which is hosting the summit fresh off a tariff firestorm with Washington. US President Donald Trump sees the grouping itself as an assault on the US currency and has threatened to impose 100 percent tariffs on BRICS nations if they work to replace the US dollar. India backs legitimate local-currency settlement, while maintaining it is against any common BRICS currency or China-centered replacement mechanism. As it walks the diplomatic tightrope, India must steer initiatives like the integration of central bank digital currencies (CBDCs) but without appearing to endorse any anti-dollar bloc.Another challenge for India is to prevent China's predominance without destabilising its bilateral relations with Beijing. For all the talk about BRICS' combined power, China enjoys a vastly asymmetrical influence with its trade, investment, manufacturing and critical mineral leverage. Wary of China's efforts to advance its own economic interests, India has not endorsed SCO’s 2030 economic roadmap and it must find a way to work with China in BRICS on shared objectives but without allowing the forum to be co-opted as a Chinese economic or geopolitical platform.This also intersects with the challenge of ensuring that an expanded grouping remains governable and cohesive, especially with countries like Pakistan and Bangladesh pursuing membership with support from Beijing. True multipolarity and consensus-driven equality within the organisation are key imperatives for India.As Jaishankar said while announcing India's summit agenda, BRICS must transition now from a forum for discussions to a platform for delivery. In that spirit, India seems focused on delivering an outcome-oriented summit with key deliverables like a unanimous BRICS declaration, logistics supply-chain cooperation framework, incubator/ startup network, development finance, cross-border payment and continued support for Indian priorities like UNSC reforms and counterterrorism.To conclude, inclusion of the African Union was not the only major takeaway from the G20 summit in 2023. Perhaps more dramatic was the last-minute consensus on Ukraine through a compromise language crafted by India, allowing a G20 declaration. India can take confidence from that diplomatic triumph, heading into another tough but potentially rewarding global summit.
Article Summary: India will host the annual BRICS summit on September 12-13 at Bharat Mandapam, returning to the venue where it held the G20 summit in 2023. This would be the 18th summit of the grouping that brings together 11 major emerging and developing economies – Brazil, Russia, India, China, South Africa, Ethiopia, UAE, Indonesia, Iran, Egypt and Saudi Arabia.

Article Title: Why Vijay's gold ring scheme may miss its September 15 launch
Article Text:
Under Vijay's gold ring scheme, every newborn delivered at a government health facility will receive a one-gram gold ring. At the current gold rate, the ring is worth around Rs 13,600.

What is the gold ring scheme?

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Tamil Nadu chief minister C Joseph Vijay's gold ring scheme, which was scheduled to be launched on September 15, shall be deferred from its expected date. The announcement comes as the CM prepares for his first official overseas visit to London. Vijay is set to meet European industrialists during the visit and pitch Tamil Nadu as an investment destination.Vijay will leave Chennai for London via Dubai on Wednesday night and is expected to stay in the UK capital for a few days. He will travel on an Emirates Airlines passenger flight.During the visit, Vijay is expected to invite European companies to set up businesses in Tamil Nadu and seek fresh investment commitments for the state. Senior officials from the industries and finance departments are also expected to travel to London. Some may leave ahead of the chief minister to prepare for his meetings with prospective investors.The visit comes soon after the ‘Vettri Tamil Nadu Investment Conclave 2026’, where the state government announced investment commitments worth Rs 1,02,514 crore through 104 memorandums of understanding (MoUs).Security and protocol arrangements for Vijay’s departure are also being finalised.A high-level Advance Security Liaison meeting is reportedly scheduled at Chennai’s old airport on Wednesday to review the arrangements.Vijay’s London visit also comes amid key political developments in Tamil Nadu. Before leaving for the UK, he is scheduled to chair a second alliance coordination meeting at the Tamilaga Vettri Kazhagam headquarters in Panaiyur.The meeting is expected to discuss the structure of the ruling alliance and post-poll coalition arrangements. A Common Minimum Programme is also on the agenda, along with discussions on a steering committee and an official name for the alliance.Invitations have reportedly been sent to all alliance partners, including Congress, VCK, IUML, MDMK, CPI and CPM. Congress, VCK, IUML and MDMK have confirmed their attendance, while the Left parties are likely to stay away.Vijay had announced the one-gram gold ring scheme ahead of the April 23 Assembly election. The initiative was planned as a symbolic gift to newborns and draws on the Tamil tradition of ‘Thaimaaman Seer’.Under the scheme, every newborn delivered at a government health facility will receive a one-gram gold ring. At the current gold rate, the ring is worth around Rs 13,600.“Through this scheme, the government assumes the role of the maaman (uncle) for every child born in its institutions, presenting a gold ring as an enduring token of welcome,” a government order said.The scheme was originally scheduled to be launched on September 15, which coincides with the birth anniversary of former chief minister C N Annadurai.It will have retrospective effect from June 22, Vijay’s birthday. The government order issued on June 23 described the initiative as a token celebrating the birth of the child, motherhood and the cultural tradition of ‘Thaimaaman’.The state has allocated around Rs 755.83 crore annually for the scheme, which will cover all newborns delivered at government institutions. There will be no restriction based on birth order and no gender-based discrimination.The Tamil Nadu Medical Services Corporation will procure the gold rings and supply them based on annual requirements. A project and programme management unit will also be established to oversee implementation and monitoring.Tamil Nadu records around 7.8 lakh deliveries each year, with institutional deliveries accounting for 99.9% of births, according to NFHS-6. Government health facilities account for nearly 4.2 lakh deliveries, or about 53% of the total.According to the state government, the average out-of-pocket expenditure for a delivery at a government hospital is Rs 1,364, compared with Rs 63,473 at a private hospital.The scheme is open to Tamil Nadu residents whose children are delivered at government institutions. Mothers will have to submit proof of residence, with documents such as ration cards, voter identity cards, Aadhaar, Labour Welfare Board identity cards, Department of Posts address cards and nativity certificates accepted.The government said the initiative was intended to combine cultural significance with public healthcare.“Gold carries profound cultural and emotional resonance in Tamil Nadu. Gifting gold to a newborn celebrates the baby’s arrival, honours the mother’s noble journey and transforms public health delivery into a source of immense community pride,” the order said.
Article Summary: Under Vijay's scheme, every newborn delivered at a government health facility will receive a one-gram gold ring. At the current gold rate, the ring is worth around Rs 13,600. Vijay is set to meet European industrialists during the visit and pitch Tamil Nadu as an investment destination.

Article Title: Silver prices crash over 40% from Rs 4 lakh/kg high to Rs 2.35 lakh, but buyers are still staying away; bigger problem yet to arrive as 2,000 tonnes ordered by Indian dealers risk piling up
Article Text:
Traders and analysts have said that the slowdown in investment demand can be seen across silver exchange-traded funds (ETFs), bars and coins.

Silver Demand Weakens

Massive stockpiling of silver

Silver’s Spectacular Fall

(Disclaimer: Recommendations and views on the stock market, or any other asset classes or personal finance management tips given by experts and analysts are their own. These opinions do not represent the views of The Times of India.)

A huge crash in silver prices should have led to a revival in demand, but investors seem to be staying away. And this has raised a fresh worry ahead of the festive season.Silver refiners and bullion dealers are seeing their inventories build up as new investment demand for the metal weakens. The situation comes even as silver prices have dropped by more than 40% from their January peak of over Rs 4 lakh per kg. Uncertainty over a possible breakthrough in the US-Iran war and concerns about subdued industrial demand have added to the pressure.In Mumbai’s spot market, silver was trading at Rs 2.35 lakh per kg earlier this week.Traders and analysts have said that the slowdown in investment demand can be seen across silver exchange-traded funds (ETFs), bars and coins. Investors who bought the metal when prices were significantly higher are now sitting on substantial losses, making them hesitant to make fresh purchases despite the steep correction in prices!Also Read | A couple sold gold for Rs 20 lakh to buy a home, another family got Rs 80 lakh for a US degree and business: How Indians are unlocking value of idle gold sitting in their lockers "Investment demand for silver ETFs, bars and coins has come down. Internationally, prices are unlikely to cross $100 per troy ounce immediately unless the US-Iran war comes to an end. Silver prices are undervalued," Chirag Sheth, global business head, Public Gold Bullion (SG) Pte told ET. "The continuous war between US and Iran has impacted the solar industry, semiconductor industry and EV industry where silver is used. "The weak demand is also creating an inventory problem for domestic players.Indian bullion dealers and refiners have reportedly placed orders for around 2,000 tonnes of silver, which is currently in transit. The additional supplies have raised concerns over a further build-up in stocks. India imports around 7,000 tonnes of silver every year."With no new investors coming in and no immediate signs of prices going up, refiners and bullion dealers are facing a problem internationally as well as in domestic markets," said James Jose, president, Precious Metals Refiners Forum.Silver prices have fallen steadily over the past seven months, following an extraordinary rally that pushed the metal more than 300% higher year-on-year. In January, silver crossed Rs 4 lakh per kg on the Multi Commodity Exchange for the first time."The market is still digesting the aftermath of the speculation-driven frenzy, and this may be prompting investors to stay away after many of them incurred significant losses," said Carsten Menke, head, Next Generation Research, Julius Baer told ET.The outlook for industrial demand is adding to the pressure, with consumption expected to weaken. "A shift to cheaper alternatives, such as aluminium and copper, has started, and the growth outlook for Chinese solar module makers, which are the biggest industrial users of silver, is not as strong anymore," Menke said.The ongoing US-Iran war has added to the negative sentiment surrounding silver. If the conflict continues for an extended period, investors may remain cautious. At the same time, expectations of weaker industrial consumption could make a rapid rebound in silver prices difficult.Despite the sharp fall, some long-term investors are once again looking at silver as a way to diversify their portfolios."The market has taken full cognisance of the marked decline in silver prices in recent days. Some investors have shaved off their allocation, while others have prepared for fresh acquisition depending on their views and goals," said Nilanjan Dey, partner, Wishlist Capital.Dey said investors who have a time horizon of five years or longer may look at buying silver ETFs in a staggered manner instead of putting in a large amount at one go. Monthly or fortnightly investments could help spread out the purchase price and reduce the impact of short-term price movements.For first-time investors looking to add precious metals to their portfolios as a diversification from equities, ETFs can provide exposure without the need to hold or manage physical silver. However, Dey warned that investors with a shorter investment horizon should not assume that the recent decline automatically makes silver an attractive buying opportunity.
Article Summary: Silver refiners and bullion dealers are seeing their inventories build up as new investment demand for the metal weakens. Silver prices have dropped by more than 40% from their January peak of over Rs 4 lakh per kg. Uncertainty over a possible breakthrough in the US-Iran war and concerns about subdued industrial demand have added to the pressure.

Article Title: Indian paratroopers train with US, Japan, France in major Indo-Pacific war games
Article Text:
US troops fire an M240B machine gun during a multilateral exercise being held in Indonesia. (Image credit: US DoW)

India Rolls Out 400th Apache Fuselage As Defence Sector Takes Off

Indian troops along with soldiers from 20 other nations are taking part in one of Indo-Pacific's largest multinational military exercises in terms of countries involved The wargames called Exercise Super Garuda Shield 2026, is nearing its end in the Indonesian archipelago, according to local media. Running from August 31 to September 11, the annual exercise has brought together 4,743 personnel who working through 12 separate training modules at multiple sites across the island chain.India's contribution has come in the form of 40 paratroopers as per reports from Indonesia. The report also mentions that Indian soldiers along with American, New Zealand and Indonesian troops participated in a joint "Special Operation Forces (SOF) Flat Range Advance Shooting" drill at the Indonesian Army's Combat Training Center in Martapura, South Sumatra. In all, 270 personnel took part in this active firing event along with 110 Indonesian troops, 80 American troops, 45 from New Zealand and 40 Indian soldiers, running through advanced live-fire drills designed to sharpen marksmanship, combat effectiveness and coordination in joint operational scenarios. The exercise wrapped up without incident.Beyond the shooting range, Indian troops also featured in the exercise's airborne segment.Indian paratroopers joined their Indonesian, American, Japanese and French counterparts in a static-line parachute exercise in which jumps were conducted from low altitudes of 1,200 feet over the Baturaja landing area in South Sumatra, one of several joint training activities designed to test how well partner militaries can operate together on short notice, as per Jakarta.Indonesian Armed Forces Commander General Agus Subiyanto said the broader exercise is meant to test operational readiness, deepen defence diplomacy and sharpen partner militaries' ability to respond to emerging security challenges, a description that captures just how far Super Garuda Shield has grown beyond a routine bilateral drill. Besides India, Indonesia and the US, participating nations this year include Australia, Japan, France, UK, Canada, South Korea, Singapore, Thailand and several other regional and partner countries, as per Indonesian media.For India, the exercise fits into a much bigger picture of strengthening ties with Indonesia under the Comprehensive Strategic Partnership. Jakarta has recently procured India's BrahMos supersonic cruise missile and become the first export customer for the Astra air-to-air missile, both signs of how far the defence relationship between the two countries has come. New Delhi and Jakarta also increasingly see eye to eye on maritime security and freedom of navigation across the Indo-Pacific, particularly around the strategically vital Malacca Strait. Multinational exercises like Super Garuda Shield continue to give India and its regional partners a working platform to build on that cooperation, one live-fire drill and parachute jump at a time.
Article Summary: Indian troops are taking part in one of Indo-Pacific's largest multinational military exercises. The wargames called Exercise Super Garuda Shield 2026, is nearing its end in the Indonesian archipelago. Running from August 31 to September 11, the annual exercise has brought together 4,743 personnel.

Article Title: ‘Special 26’ in Mumbai: Sacked driver teams up with I-T officials to target ex-employer in fake raid
Article Text:
Six individuals, including three women, were arrested by Andheri police for a fake raid.





MUMBAI: In a Akshay Kumar-starrer Special 26-style plot, a sacked driver allegedly teamed up with two Income Tax officials and others to conduct a fake raid at his former employer’s office in Mumbai and demand Rs 1 crore. The extortion bid was foiled after the company owner asked the alleged raiding team to produce authorisation documents.Andheri police have arrested 10 people in connection with the July 17 incident, including two serving I-T officials. Police said the operation was masterminded by former company driver Santosh Khopatkar, 37, who was sacked about three months before the alleged raid and wanted revenge against his former employer.The fake raid was conducted at Two M Ophthotronics Pvt Ltd in Sahar Cargo Estate, Chakala. Police registered an FIR on September 4 following a complaint by company owner Rajkumar Kandasami.Kandasami told police that his employees called him saying I-T officials had raided the office. Two men in plain clothes later approached Kandasami and his wife near their home, introduced themselves as I-T officials and displayed an identity card.They allegedly forced the couple into an aggregator cab and took them to the office.Sub-inspector Rohan Surve said the accused questioned employees, examined company documents and took away the mobile phones of Kandasami, his wife and staff. They allegedly produced a purported search warrant and obtained Kandasami’s signature on it.The group questioned Kandasami about cash transactions, threatened him with a substantial penalty and offered to settle the purported tax case for Rs 1 crore. However, Kandasami asked them to produce authorisation documents for the raid. The alleged raiding team could not produce any and left empty-handed after around three hours.Kandasami subsequently checked with his chartered accountant and found that the Income Tax department had not ordered any raid at his company.Police said their investigation revealed that Khopatkar had provided the tip-off about the company. He had allegedly approached the I-T officials for help in raiding his former employer after being sacked.The two I-T officials arrested in the case are inspector Sureshkumar Mishra, 57, posted at the Piramal Chamber office in Lalbaug, and tax assistant Sunil Gore, 59, posted at the Kautilya Bhavan office in BKC.Police said Mishra and Gore had allegedly conducted a similar raid on a company in Manpada and demanded Rs 65 lakh.Those arrested earlier in the Chakala case include Khopatkar, Vinay More, 37, Prem Sabnani, 50, Pragnya M, Reshma Shyamrao Warang, 41, and Shabina Shaikh, 48.DCP (West Zone-3) Datta Nalawade said police also took custody of Jitendra More of Thane and Ashok Shinde of Vile Parle West on Thursday. The two were already in judicial custody in connection with the Manpada case.A team led by senior inspector Umesh Machindar, inspector Atul Nikam, assistant inspector Ramdas Kadam and sub-inspectors Rohan Surve and Rameshwar Karpe analysed call records, mobile numbers, dump data, location details and CCTV footage from government and private cameras.Investigators are examining the seized phones for calls, chats, WhatsApp messages and financial transactions to establish the alleged conspiracy, identify other associates and determine the role of each accused.
Article Summary: Andheri police have arrested 10 people in connection with the July 17 incident, including two serving I-T officials. Police said the operation was masterminded by former company driver Santosh Khopatkar, 37, who was sacked about three months before the alleged raid.

Article Title: Indiramma Housing Scheme: 59,000 hut dwellers to get priority in Indiramma Ph-II: Ponguleti
Article Text:
Hyderabad





: Housing minister Ponguleti Srinivas Reddy on Thursday said 59,000 hut dwellers would be prioritised for Indiramma houses in the second phase of the scheme.Responding to questions raised by MLAs Manohar Reddy, Rajagopal Reddy, Medipally Satyam, Akbaruddin Owaisi, Venkatrami Reddy and other members in the assembly, the minister said the state govt would not adopt a policy of shifting poor families 30 to 40 km away from their sources of livelihood.He said Indiramma houses were being sanctioned by treating each assembly constituency as a unit, to provide houses that uphold the dignity of the poor even in areas where an acre of land is valued at ₹150 crore to ₹200 crore.The minister said complete transparency was being maintained in the selection of beneficiaries. Officials were physically verifying every beneficiary selected through the draw by visiting their homes. He made it clear in the assembly that if persons belonging to other constituencies were found to have been selected, their names would be removed from the list.Ponguleti said there was no precedent of any state or the Union govt providing ₹5 lakh in financial assistance free of cost for house construction, while Telangana was extending such support under the Indiramma housing scheme. He noted that several members had suggested that ₹5 lakh was inadequate and said the govt would examine the issue positively.“Approximately ₹22,500 crore will be required for the 4.5 lakh houses sanctioned in the first phase, around ₹11,000 crore for the 2.5 lakh houses in the second phase, and approximately ₹5,500 crore for one lakh houses in urban areas. The govt will have to bear more than ₹40,000 crore for around eight lakh houses under the two phases alone,” he said.Ponguleti said that around 3,200 houses that had been taken up with govt approval during the first phase but had subsequently stalled due to minor deficiencies in construction had been regularised and cleared. Steps were being taken to ensure that payments to all such beneficiaries were released by the end of this week, he said.The minister criticised the previous practice of allocating houses based on political considerations and said the present govt was sanctioning houses solely on the basis of eligibility. He added that steps were being taken to identify govt lands earmarked for the poor during the erstwhile united Andhra Pradesh, as well as lands that had been acquired but not allotted.He said instructions had been issued to district collectors to ensure that these sites were allotted to eligible beneficiaries in their respective constituencies within a month.
Article Summary: Housing minister Ponguleti Srinivas Reddy said 59,000 hut dwellers would be prioritised for Indiramma houses in the second phase of the scheme. He said the state govt would not adopt a policy of shifting poor families 30 to 40 km away from their sources of livelihood.
